Storing a user’s login token and bank details directly in the browser’s local storage is unsafe – anyone who can open that browser (or the device) could read those secrets, and if the browser data is cached or corrupted the user could lose money. The safest way is to keep the token on your server and only keep short‑lived, non‑sensitive IDs in the browser. For bank details you should store them in a secure server‑side database (with proper encryption and access controls) and never expose the raw data in the client code.
